cells.tense: The gathering is happening now and you are the one at the desk doing it.
cells.ask: Write where you are steering in one honest paragraph, then read it aloud to one person whose view you trust.
cells.core:
Strands that used to pull in different directions are lining up, and what you do next is starting to have one direction instead of three. You sat with the pieces long enough that they sorted, and the decisions you make lately tend to hold, because the deciding and the aim point the same way.

You are not forcing this. That is worth noticing, because it is easy to treat a settled mind as ordinary. Stay at the desk while it's working. It is a flowing thing, not something you can bank. There is more here you could put into words than you have bothered to.
cells.sheetLine: Your thoughts are lining up and you're steering by them.
cells.verb: gathering scattered strands of thought into one line you can steer by
cells.place: the star you steer by, above the busyness

cells.tense: You are gathering ahead of a future you keep trying to write before it arrives.
cells.ask: Close whatever you are writing and take one aimable next step today, no plan beyond it.
cells.core:
You are gathering so far ahead that the gathering has become the thing. There is a version of this in your head where every strand is finally arranged and only then can you move, so you keep pulling more threads in and nothing gets walked. The next move keeps getting postponed by the next thought.

What you are steering by is supposed to orient you, not wait for you to finish sorting. You know enough now to take one step, and the step is the only thing that will tell you whether the arrangement is right. The danger isn't the plan being wrong. It's that planning has replaced moving. One step today, aimed where you claim you're going.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you a while back.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you want and tell one safe person about it this week, out loud, plainly.
cells.core:
The pulling-together stopped a while back and you have not been at the desk. Not busy. Absent. There is a pile of thoughts from that time that did not get gathered, and you have been leaving it where it fell and calling yourself fine with it.

What you want has not gone away, either. It is quiet in you and you keep it that way, because naming it out loud once did not go well and you have been careful since. Careful is not the same as settled. The desk is still there. It does not need you to be ready. It needs you to sit down and let someone hear what you actually want, without the case for it attached.

cells.tense: You are already writing the direction and calling it something that happened to you.
cells.ask: Tell one person about a choice you made that they credit to circumstance, and say plainly that you made it.
cells.core:
You talk about your direction like it arrived on its own. It shifted, things lined up — as if the lining up happened without you at the desk. It didn't. You have been choosing what to steer by for a while now, in what you say yes to and what you quietly let go, and those choices are already steering the life you're in.

The choosing is yours and you have been handing it to circumstance. That is a load off, in one way, and a loss, in another. You don't have to announce anything to anyone. Just stop filing your own steering under luck. Someone close to you can hold the real version, if you let them hear one of those choices named as yours.

attempts.check: Unsupported claim: that the person's scattered thoughts resolve into one coherent strategy, and that following it feels like clean direction. A reader could reasonably say the gathering is still real work and nothing has settled yet, or that it settled without effort. The ask survives being wrong because it names an act — write it whole and honestly, then let one person read it — which teaches something even if the clarity was always there or never was, and lives on what the writing turns up. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'you already know where you're going', so it is gone; the cell only says the drawing-together keeps happening and the following has begun.
